descriptionChirho: The common noun for water (Greek ὕδωρ), encompassing all NT uses: natural water (seas, rivers, wells, rain), water for purification and ritual washing, baptismal water, and drinking water. All grammatical cases and numbers (singular, plural, nominative, genitive, dative, accusative) and prepositional constructions ('with water,' 'in water,' 'of water') refer to the same substance. Uniformly translated: Spanish 'agua/aguas,' Arabic 'مَاءِ/مَاءَ,' Hindi 'पानी,' Korean '물,' Swahili 'maji.' The instrumental uses ('with water' for baptism) represent contextual application, not a distinct lexical sense.
